did_you_know.text: Did you know? This chapter emphasizes centralized worship: slaughtering cattle, sheep, and goats is connected with bringing the offering to the Tent of Meeting, rather than practicing private worship in the open field.

Did you know? The word se'irim is related to se'ir, meaning “goat,” and may refer to goat-like beings in ancient popular belief. The prohibition teaches that Israelite worship was meant to be directed only to God.
Did you know? The phrase “the life of the flesh is in the blood” reflects the biblical view that blood represents the power of life, and therefore it was dedicated to the altar rather than eaten.
Did you know? Covering the blood with earth means that hunting animals, not only offering sacrifices at the sanctuary, also required a ritual response to blood.

Did you know? Impurity caused by eating an animal carcass or a torn animal was temporary, lasting until evening; washing the body and clothes allowed the person to return to a state of purity afterward.
